newsitem.title: UK: BT rises as traders pick 1997 outperformers.
newsitem.headline: BT rises as traders pick 1997 outperformers.

text.p: British Telecommunications' shares rose to near year-highs on Friday as fund managers earmarked the stock as a one of next year's top performers amid further deregulation in the sector, analysts said.
Also boosted by a sharply stronger FTSE 100, the stock rose five pence to 403.5p by 1300 GMT, with 13.7 million shares changing hands.
"As the (telecommunications) market gets closer to deregulation, those most atuned to competition -- the leaner companies -- will benefit," said a telecoms analyst at brokers HSBC James Capel.
Shares in Vodafone Group, Britain's biggest mobile 'phone company and Securicor Group, joint owners with BT of mobile 'phone group Cellnet, also strengthened.
"We have a positive feel about BT, Vodafone and Securicor," the analyst added.
"It is the time of the year when lots of fund managers are looking to next year. Everyone is taking a step back and looking at the broader picture."
Natwest Securities said it had included BT in its top 15 stocks for 1997.
But one analyst at ABN AMRO said 90 percent of the movement in the stock was attributable to the general rise in the top 100 companies' shares, of which BT is a weighty component.

He added that the opening up of the international telephone market to 44 new competitors, confirmed on Thursday, may prove to be the leverage necessary to approve a proposed $20 billion merger between BT and America's MCI Comunications Corp.
Regulatory clearance of the deal, that has been trumpeted as the biggest trans-Atlantic merger in history, partly hinges on whether the UK telecoms market is deemed to be as open as that of the U.S.
